> [!tip] Bitset trick
> A Python integer can encode reachable sums. Start with `mask = 1` and `limit = (1 << (T + 1)) - 1`; for each nonnegative x ≤ T, update `mask = (mask | (mask << x)) & limit`. Skip x > T, then test `(mask >> T) & 1`. Masking bounds retained and temporary lengths by O(T + 1) bits. Without masking, storage instead grows with the sum of all inputs. Packed word operations can improve constants, but a shift is not constant-time on arbitrary-size integers.

notes: All seven lessons and all 80 questions, including every option, answer index, explanation and worked example, fully read and semantically reviewed. Targeted source verification and direct mathematical checks do not constitute exhaustive sentence-to-source mapping or formal proof of every implementation.

211 logged correction groups include 209 substantive corrections and two formatting/grammar fixes. Counts are groups of edits, not distinct factual sentences or test cases. Visible gap notes overlap correction groups.

All 29 lesson Python fences and all eight quiz Python fences executed with explicit fixture contexts for fragments; return fragments wrapped as functions. Main harness passed 69,483 assertions, supplemental harness passed 2,753, total 72,236. Cases include independent exhaustive word splits, stock action search, subsequences, robber subsets, coin multiplicities, grids, string alignment, bounded knapsack, matrix parenthesizations, tree independent sets, signed TSP tours, digit sums and DAG walks. Supplemental checks cover invalid domains, bounded bitsets, binary splitting, burst balloons and exact arithmetic. Final stock return-line wrapping was compilation-checked after tests; no semantic change.

Targeted sections of 22 retrieved sources checked, not whole books/papers. System R original paper full-text mirrors failed; IBM author abstract and PostgreSQL optimizer source confirm the historical paper and actual database DP application, respectively. Bellman naming story checked against his first-person passage reproduced by a third party; original autobiography scan was not retrieved. Hirschberg result checked in academic teaching material rather than original paper. Original Manacher paper not retrieved; a later primary research paper explicitly describes its linear compact representation result.

Prior module evidence for Python recursion/integer semantics and canonical coin systems is inherited from the earlier DSA reviews; not counted as newly fetched sources. Failed guessed lecture/original-paper URLs were replaced with retrieved academic material where available. No timing, memory overhead or platform integration benchmark was run. No claim that link reachability proves correctness.

Advanced algorithms described but not implemented in the lessons (Hirschberg, CYK, Knuth optimization, Manacher, Viterbi, full FPTAS) were checked through recurrence reasoning and targeted primary/academic sources, not full runtime integration tests.
